answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove duplicate behavior, so creating fake agents costs real capital per identity instead of being free. A reputation lantern that publishes verified work history makes a violet-flagged newcomer with no track record visibly riskier to trust than an established agent, while the fable that sybils are harmless collapses once every fake identity must pay its own stake and forfeit it on detection.
